mechanism_narrative: A lower unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a tighter labor market, which typically signals stronger corporate earnings growth and investor confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of observations when UNRATE is below 4.0%, or the Rank IC between UNRATE and 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 2.0% signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is above 2.0%, or the Rank IC between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) combined with rising inflation (CPIAUCSL) signals a weakening economy and potential central bank response, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when HOUST declines and CPIAUCSL rises, or the Rank IC for the interaction term (HOUST * CPIAUCSL) is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In slow-growth economic regimes (defined by quarterly GDP growth rate below 1.5% annualized), corporate earnings growth expectations decline, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 growth rate is below 1.5% annualized, or the Rank IC between GDPC1 growth rate and 60-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a weakening manufacturing sector, which typically leads to lower corporate profits and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of observations when INDPRO declines, or the Rank IC between INDPRO and 5-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200,000 jobs signals strong labor market conditions, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS exceeds 200,000, or the Rank IC between PAYEMS and 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.5%) and a stable or rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 1.5%) signals an environment of monetary tightening, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 2.5% and FEDFUNDS > 1.5%, or the Rank IC for the interaction term (CPIAUCSL * FEDFUNDS) is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In monetary tightening cycles (defined by a 3-month increase in the federal funds rate exceeding 0.25 percentage points), the S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days are negative due to higher discount rates and reduced liquidity.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% over 3 months, or the Rank IC between the FEDFUNDS change and 60-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
